subject.title: [Bug]: clearUnboundScopes strips operator scopes unconditionally for non-local token-auth clients

question: Should non-local device-less WebSocket clients authenticated with a shared token/password retain operator scopes by default, or should trusted remote/headless deployments use an explicit token-scope/device policy?
rationale: Current source and docs deliberately clear device-less shared-token scopes except for named local trust paths, while the report asks to broaden remote token-auth behavior on a Gateway authorization boundary.

options.title: Explicit Token-Scope Policy
options.body: Keep remote device-less scope clearing as the default and land a bounded configured token-scope or device-token path for trusted headless deployments.

options.title: Restore Remote Token Retention
options.body: Treat valid shared token/password auth as enough for non-local WebSocket operators to retain requested scopes by default, accepting the broader bearer-token trust boundary.

options.title: Document Unsupported Default
options.body: Keep the current default and document that remote WebSocket operator clients must pair or use a maintainer-approved token-scope path instead of retaining self-declared scopes.

recommendation.title: Explicit Token-Scope Policy
recommendation.body: Keep remote device-less scope clearing as the default and land a bounded configured token-scope or device-token path for trusted headless deployments.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the open tokenScopes implementation candidate and has recent history on the default-token scope policy.
